qs.q: If a food particle is placed near the osculum of a sponge then it will -
o: Be ingested first and then thrown out through ostia
qs.s: Water exits sponges through the osculum, so any particle placed near it will be blown or thrown away by the outgoing water current.

qs.q: Bath sponge is common name of:
qs.s: Euspongia is commonly known as the bath sponge.

qs.q: Which one of the following is Coelenterate?
qs.s: Sea fan (Gorgonia) belongs to the phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria).

qs.q: Which animal do not possess larval stage in its life cycle?
qs.s: Pheretima (earthworm) shows direct development without any larval stage.

qs.q: Which of the following is an Annelid?
qs.s: Sea mouse (Aphrodite) is a marine annelid.

qs.q: Which of the following characteristic is shared by all arthropods?
qs.s: The presence of jointed appendages is a defining characteristic shared by all arthropods.

qs.q: Members of phylum Arthropoda lack one of the following feature :
o: Usually a close type of blood vascular system
qs.s: Arthropods possess an open type of blood vascular system, not a closed type.

qs.q: Cockroach, house fly and mosquitoes are insect because they have :-
o: Chitinous exoskeleton and body divided into head and cephalothorax
Six legs, compound eyes and body divided into head, thorax and abdomen
Segmented body with jointed feet and chitinous exoskeleton
Three pairs of legs, one pair of antennae and flame cells
qs.s: Insects are characterized by having three pairs of legs (six legs), compound eyes, and a body divided into head, thorax, and abdomen.

qs.q: Which of the following animal is considered as "Living fossil"?
qs.s: Limulus (king crab) is considered a living fossil because it has remained virtually unchanged over millions of years.

qs.q: Select the economically important insect:
qs.s: Apis (honey bee) is an economically important insect producing honey and wax.

qs.q: Which animal has visceral hump ?
qs.s: Pila belongs to Mollusca, which possess a soft body covered by a mantle and a distinct visceral hump.

qs.q: Which mollusca is called tusk shell?
qs.s: Dentalium is commonly known as the tusk shell due to its shape.

qs.q: Secretion of shell in molluscs take place by:
qs.s: The mantle (pallium) is a fold of skin that secretes the calcareous shell in molluscs.

qs.q: Which of the following characteristic is not of phylum mollusca?
o: Soft body covered usually by a shell
qs.s: Molluscs are unsegmented soft-bodied animals.

qs.q: The most characteristic feature of molluscs is the presence of:
qs.s: The presence of a soft mantle covering the visceral mass is a unique key feature of molluscs.

qs.q: Open type of blood vascular system and presence of haemocyanin pigment are the characters of:
qs.s: Molluscs typically have an open circulatory system and use haemocyanin as a respiratory pigment.

qs.q: Member of Echinodermata has a specific system, which is not found in other phylum, it is:
qs.s: The water vascular system (ambulacral system) is a unique characteristic feature of echinoderms.

qs.q: Segmentation of body is not represented in:
qs.s: Sepia is a mollusc and lacks body segmentation.

qs.q: Which of the following is not related with Echinodermata ?
qs.s: Parapodia are locomotory appendages found in annelids like Nereis, not in echinoderms.

qs.q: Locomotory organs of echinoderms are :-
qs.s: Tube feet (podia) connected to the water vascular system serve as locomotory organs in echinoderms.

qs.q: Absence of excretory organs, great power of regeneration and exclusively marine animals belongs to the phylum :-
qs.s: Echinoderms lack specialized excretory organs, are exclusively marine, and show high regenerative capabilities.

qs.q: Stomochord (Buccal diverticulum) is present in:
qs.s: Balanoglossus (Hemichordata) possesses a rudiment in the collar region called stomochord.

qs.q: Which of the following character does not belong to Arthropoda?
qs.s: Arthropods feature an open circulatory system rather than a closed one.

qs.q: Chiton is included in phylum:
qs.s: Chiton belongs to the phylum Mollusca (class Polyplacophora).

qs.q: Coxal glands are the excretory organ of:
qs.s: Scorpions (arachnids) utilize coxal glands for excretion.

qs.q: Most of the adult insects have six legs and:
o: Two antennae and two or four wings
qs.s: Insects typically possess one pair of antennae (2 total) and one or two pairs of wings (2 or 4 total).

qs.q: In Hydra, waste material of food digestion and nitrogenous waste material removed respectively from:
qs.s: Undigested waste is ejected through the mouth (gastrovascular cavity opening) and nitrogenous waste diffuses across the body wall.

qs.q:
Given below are four matchings of an animal and its kind of respiratory organ:
A. Silver fish - Trachea
B. Scorpion - Book lung
C. Sea squirt - Pharyngeal gills
D. Dolphin - Skin
The correct matchings are :-
qs.s: Silver fish respires via trachea, scorpion via book lungs, and sea squirt via pharyngeal gills; dolphins are mammals and breathe via lungs.

qs.q: In contrast to Annelids, the Platyhelminthes show:
qs.s: Platyhelminthes are acoelomate (lacking a coelom/body cavity), whereas annelids are true coelomates.

qs.q: The canal system is characteristic feature of:
qs.s: The canal system is a characteristic body organisation feature in sponges (Porifera).

qs.q: Which of the following is pseudoceolomate?
qs.s: Ascaris belongs to Aschelminthes, which are pseudocoelomates.

qs.q: Sycon belongs to a group of animals, which are best described as:
o: Multicellular having tissue organization, but no body cavity
qs.s: Sycon is a sponge (Porifera) exhibiting cellular level of organization without true tissue formation.

qs.q: Which one of the following phyla is correctly matched with its general characteristics ?
o: Porifera Cellular level of organisation and external fertilisation
Hemichordata - Coelomates and closed circulatory system
qs.s: Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomate animals and are typically dioecious (unisexual).

qs.q: Which one of the following is a matching pair of a body feature and the animal possessing it?
qs.s: Obelia exhibits alternation of generations (metagenesis) between polypoid and medusoid forms.

qs.q: One of the following animals is not hermaphrodite :
qs.s: Ascaris is dioecious (sexes are separate), whereas earthworms, leeches, and tapeworms are hermaphroditic.

qs.q: In Annelids formation of larva is usually absent but when present the larva is called:
qs.s: When larval stages occur in annelids, the characteristic larva is the trochophore larva.

qs.q: Excretion in most Annelids take place by:
qs.s: Nephridia are the excretory and osmoregulatory organs in annelids.

qs.q: Sea-anemone belongs to phylum:
qs.s: Sea anemone (Adamsia) belongs to phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria).

qs.q: Skeleton is made up of ________ in porifera.
qs.s: The skeleton of sponges is supported by calcareous or siliceous spicules, spongin fibres, or both.

qs.q: Find the odd
qs.s: Sea horse is a chordate (osteichthyes fish), while sea fan, sea cucumber, and sea lily are invertebrates.

qs.q: Which animal has only cylindrical form?
qs.s: Adamsia and Hydra exist exclusively in the polypoid (cylindrical) form.

qs.q: Which animal is umbrella-shaped and free swiming?
qs.s: Aurelia, commonly known as jelly-fish, is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming (medusa form).

qs.q: Corals have a skeleton composed of
qs.s: The hard skeletal structures of corals are composed of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃).

qs.q: Identify the animal shown in diagram [Figure omitted]
qs.s: The diagram illustrates Pleurobrachia, a ctenophore showing comb plates.

qs.q: Choose the correct combination of the given option?
qs.s: Calotes is correctly matched with its common name, garden lizard.

qs.q: Which one of the following mammalia live in water?
qs.s: Blue whale (Balaenoptera) is an aquatic mammal.

qs.q: The distinguishing feature of all chordates is:
qs.s: The presence of a dorsal supportive rod called notochord is the fundamental defining feature of chordates.

qs.q: Chordates possess :
o: Dorsal nerve cord placed below gut
Single hollow nerve cord placed dorsal to gut
Single, solid and ventral nerve cord
qs.s: Chordates possess a single, hollow, dorsal nerve cord situated above the alimentary canal.

qs.q: In vertebrates, the notochord :
o: Is partially replaced by vertebral column
Is completely replaced by vertebral column
Is partially or fully replaced by vertebral column
qs.s: In vertebrates, the embryonic notochord is replaced either partially or completely by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in adults.

qs.q: Which one is the distinguishing feature of all vertebrates?
o: An internal bony or cartilagenous skeleton
qs.s: All vertebrates possess an internal endoskeleton made of cartilage or bone.

qs.q: Which one of the following amphibia is common toad?
qs.s: Bufo is commonly known as the toad.

qs.q: Which of the following group of animals have a constant body temperature?
qs.s: Aves (birds) and Mammalia are homeothermic (warm-blooded) animals capable of maintaining constant body temperature.

qs.q: Which is poikilothermic animal?
qs.s: Tortoise is a reptile and thus poikilothermic (cold-blooded), whereas birds and mammals are homeothermic.

qs.q: Which of the following is not the feature of snakes ?
qs.s: Snakes are limbless reptiles.

qs.q: Which of the following groups includes Endothermic animals (Homothermal):
qs.s: Whale and bat (mammals) and pigeon (bird) are homoiothermal (endothermic).

qs.q: Number of cranial nerves in a crocodile is:
qs.s: Crocodiles, like all reptiles, birds, and mammals, possess 12 pairs of cranial nerves.

qs.q: Mostly birds are :
qs.s: Birds excrete nitrogenous waste as uric acid (uricotelic) and lay eggs (oviparous).

qs.q: The primitive characters of Duck billed platypus suggest that it :
o: Shows the stage between aves and mammals
Shows the stage between reptiles and birds
Shows the stage between reptiles and mammals
qs.s: Duck-billed platypus is an egg-laying mammal sharing features of both reptiles and mammals.

qs.q: Find out correct statement :
o: All amphibians lay eggs in water
qs.s: Amphibians require an aquatic environment to lay eggs, making egg-laying in water universal among them.

qs.q: Oviparous animal is:
qs.s: Cobra is an egg-laying (oviparous) reptile.

qs.q: Characteristic of Corvus is:
qs.s: Corvus (crow) is unisexual and exhibits distinct sexual dimorphism.

qs.q: Which of the following is a "Lizard- bird"?
qs.s: Archaeopteryx represents a transitional fossil having reptilian (lizard) and avian (bird) features.

qs.q: Uropygial or preen glands occur in :
qs.s: Preen or uropygial oil glands are situated at the base of the tail in birds.

qs.q: The character found only in birds is :
qs.s: The presence of feathers is an exclusive diagnostic feature unique to birds (Aves).

qs.q: Which of the following characters is not related to Aves?
o: Homiothermy and presence of oil glands in skin
Female genital organs of both sides functional
Female genital organs of one sides functional
qs.s: In female birds, usually only the left ovary and oviduct are functional to reduce body weight for flight.

qs.q: Muscular diaphragm is found in:
qs.s: A muscular diaphragm separating thoracic and abdominal cavities is a unique feature of mammals.

qs.q: Whales are included in the same taxonomic class as:
qs.s: Whales and gorillas both belong to the class Mammalia.

qs.q: Which of the following group of vertebrates have dicondylic skull?
qs.s: Amphibians and mammals possess two occipital condyles (dicondylic skull).

qs.q: Hair are not found in adult whale, its body temperature is regulated by:
qs.s: Whales maintain body heat through a thick subcutaneous insulating layer of fat called blubber.

qs.q: Two chambered heart is the feature of :
qs.s: Fishes (Pisces) have a 2-chambered heart consisting of one atrium and one ventricle.

qs.q: Which of the following animals have character of both reptiles and mammals?
qs.s: Ornithorhynchus (platypus) is a prototherian mammal exhibiting reptilian and mammalian features.

qs.q: An egg laying mammal is:
qs.s: Platypus (Ornithorhynchus) is an egg-laying (oviparous) mammal.

qs.q: Presence of gills in the tadpole of frog indicates that:
o: Fishes evolved from frog like ancestors
Frogs will have gills in future
Fishes were amphibious in the past
qs.s: The gill-bearing larval stage in amphibians reflects evolutionary development from aquatic, gilled ancestor organisms.

qs.q: Hollow air filled bones (pneumatic bones) occur in:
qs.s: Birds (Aves) have long, hollow pneumatic bones containing air cavities to aid flight.

qs.q: Which of the following character is not found in all the chordates?
qs.s: The diaphragm is a characteristic unique to mammals, not all chordates.

qs.q: In which of the following animal post anal tail is found :
qs.s: Snake is a chordate, and a post-anal tail is a primary characteristic feature of chordates.

qs.q: In which of the following notochord is present in embryonic stage:
qs.s: All chordates possess a notochord during at least some phase of their embryonic development.

qs.q: Axolotl larva is the name of larva of:
qs.s: Axolotl is the larval form of Ambystoma / Salamandra that exhibits neoteny.

qs.q: Most favourable land adaptation in reptiles is:
qs.s: Epidermal scales reduce water loss through desiccation, enabling successful terrestrial living in reptiles.

qs.q: Ichthyophis belongs to :
qs.s: Ichthyophis is a limbless amphibian (Apoda/Gymnophiona).

qs.q: Air sacs connected to lungs supplement respiration in:
qs.s: Birds have air sacs connected to their lungs to supplement efficiency in respiration.

qs.q: Which of the following reptile is non-poisonous ?
qs.s: Python is a non-venomous constrictor reptile.

qs.q: Tailed amphibian is:
qs.s: Salamandra belongs to order Urodela, characterized by the presence of a tail in adults.

qs.q: Monocondylar, Poikilothermal animals are:
qs.s: Reptiles have a monocondylar skull and are poikilothermic (cold-blooded).

qs.q: Which one of the following is a true fish ?
qs.s: Cat fish is a true bony fish (Osteichthyes); cray fish, jelly fish, and silver fish are non-vertebrates.

qs.q: Corpus callosum is found in the brain of:
qs.s: Corpus callosum is a transverse tract of nerve fibers connecting cerebral hemispheres found exclusively in mammals such as the elephant.

qs.q: One of the following is a very unique feature of the mammalian body:
qs.s: A muscular diaphragm separating the thoracic and abdominal cavities is unique to mammals.

qs.q: Which is the smallest taxonomic group having cranium, vetebral column, ventral heart, pulmonary respiration and two pairs of legs ?
qs.s: Tetrapoda includes all four-limbed vertebrates possessing lungs and cranium.

qs.q: Which of the following has no teeth in its mouth?
qs.s: Tortoises lack teeth; their jaws are covered by horny beak-like structures.

qs.q: Feathers of birds are modified:
qs.s: Feathers are evolutionary modifications of reptilian epidermal scales.

qs.q: Identify the animal - [Figure omitted]
qs.s: The diagram corresponds to Ascidia, a tunicated urochordate.

qs.q: Notochord is present only in larval tail of:
qs.s: In Urochordata (tunicates), the notochord is present only in the larval tail stage.

qs.q: Vertebrates have ventral muscular heart with ________ chambers.
qs.s: Vertebrate species possess ventral muscular hearts with 2, 3, or 4 chambers depending on the class.

qs.q: Larve of ________ after metamorphosis return to the ocean.
qs.s: Lampreys (Petromyzon) undergo anadromous migration to spawn in freshwater, and their larvae return to the sea after metamorphosis.

qs.q: Air bladder is absent in
qs.s: Dogfish (Scoliodon) is a cartilaginous fish (Chondrichthyes) and lacks an air bladder.

qs.q: Sea horse is
qs.s: Sea horse (Hippocampus) is a marine bony fish.

qs.q: Which group of vertebrates have characteristic features the presence of feathers and most of them can fly ?
qs.s: Feathers and flight capability are characteristic features of birds (Aves).

qs.q: Which class name refers to their creeping or crawling mode of locomotion (Latin, repere or reptum, to creep or crawl)?
qs.s: Reptilia is derived from Latin 'repere' meaning to creep or crawl.

qs.q: Which one of the following living organisms completely lacks a cell wall?
qs.s: Sea-fan (Gorgonia) is an animal (Cnidaria) and lacks a cell wall completely.

qs.q: Select the Taxon mentioned that represents both marine and fresh water species:
qs.s: Phylum Cnidaria contains both marine species (e.g., Physalia, Aurelia) and freshwater species (e.g., Hydra).

qs.q: Planaria possess high capacity of:
qs.s: Planaria (Platyhelminthes) shows a remarkable high power of regeneration.

qs.q: A marine cartilaginous fish that can produce electric current is:
qs.s: Torpedo is an electric ray fish capable of generating electric discharge from modified muscles.

qs.q: Which of the following animals is not viviparous?
qs.s: Platypus (Ornithorhynchus) is an oviparous (egg-laying) mammal.

qs.q:
Which of the following represents the correct combination without any exception?
(1) Chondrichthyes - Mouth ventral, gills without operculum; skin with placoid scales; persistent notochord
(2) Cyclostomata - Sucking and circular mouth; jaws absent, integument without scales; paired appendages
(3) Aves - Body covered with feathers; skin moist and glandular; fore-limbs form wings; lungs with air sacs
(4) Mammalia - Mammary gland; hair on body; pinnae; two pairs of Limbs
qs.s: All Chondrichthyes consistently possess a ventral mouth, gills without opercula, placoid scales, and persistent notochord.

qs.q: Metagenesis refers to :
o: Presence of a segmented body and parthenogenetic mode of reproduction
Alternation of generation between asexual and sexual phases of an organism
Occurrence of a drastic change in form during post-embryonic development
qs.s: Metagenesis is the alternation of generations between asexual polypoid and sexual medusoid phases in coelenterates like Obelia.

qs.q: Which one of the following animals has two separate circulatory pathways ?
qs.s: Whale is a mammal possessing a 4-chambered heart with complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated double circulation pathways.

qs.q: Body having meshwork of cells, internal cavities lined with food filtering flagellated cells and indirect development are the characteristics of phylum:
qs.s: Porifera show a cellular meshwork structure with internal cavities lined by choanocytes (flagellated collar cells).

qs.q: A jawless fish, which lays eggs in fresh water and whose ammocoetes larvae after metamorphosis return to the ocean is:
qs.s: Petromyzon (lamprey) is an anadromous jawless cyclostome whose larvae undergo metamorphosis and return to the ocean.

qs.q: Which of the following characteristic features always holds true for the corresponding group of animals?
o: Possess a mouth with an upper and a lower jaw - Chordata
3 chambered heart with one incompletely divided ventricle - Reptilia
qs.s: All members of Chondrichthyes exclusively feature a cartilaginous endoskeleton without exception.

qs.q: Which one of the following characteristics is not shared by birds and mammals ?
qs.s: Birds are uniformly oviparous, whereas mammals are mostly viviparous, so viviparity is not shared.

qs.q: Choose the correct statement.
o: All reptiles have a three-chambered heart.
All pisces have gills covered by an operculum.
All cyclostomes do not possess jaws and paired fins.
qs.s: Cyclostomes are characterized by being jawless (Agnatha) and lacking paired fins.

qs.q: An important characteristic that Hemichordates share with Chordates is:
qs.s: Hemichordates share pharyngeal gill slits with chordates for respiration.

qs.q: Which among these is the correct combination of aquatic mammals ?
qs.s: Whales, dolphins, and seals are all air-breathing aquatic mammals.

qs.q: In case of poriferans, the spongocoel is lined with flagellated cells called:
qs.s: Spongocoel and canals of poriferans are lined by special flagellated cells called choanocytes.

qs.q: Which of the following animals does not undergo metamorphosis ?
qs.s: Earthworm exhibits direct development without larval stages or metamorphosis.

qs.q: Identify the vertebrate group of animals characterized by crop and gizzard in its digestive sytstem.
qs.s: The digestive tract of Aves (birds) includes specialized additional chambers named crop and gizzard.

qs.q: Which one of these animals is not a homeotherm?
qs.s: Chelone (turtle) is a reptile and therefore poikilothermic (cold-blooded).

qs.q:
Match the following organisms with their respective characteristics :
(a) Pila - (iii) Radula
(b) Bombyx - (iv) Malpighian tubules
(c) Pleurobrachia - (ii) Comb plates
(d) Taenia - (i) Flame cells
Select the correct option from the following:
qs.s: Pila has radula, Bombyx excretes via Malpighian tubules, Pleurobrachia has comb plates, and Taenia excretes using flame cells.

qs.q:
Consider following features:
(a) Organ system level of organisation
(b) Bilateral symmetry
(c) True coelomates with segmentation of body
Select the correct option of animal groups which possess all the above characteristics.
qs.s: Annelida, Arthropoda, and Chordata display organ-system organization, bilateral symmetry, true coelom, and metameric body segmentation.

qs.q:
Match the following genera with their respective phylum:
(a) Ophiura - (iii) Echinodermata
(b) Physalia - (iv) Coelenterata
(c) Pinctada - (i) Mollusca
(d) Planaria - (ii) Platyhelminthes
Select the correct option:
qs.s: Ophiura belongs to Echinodermata, Physalia to Coelenterata, Pinctada to Mollusca, and Planaria to Platyhelminthes.

qs.q: Which of the following animals are true coelomates with bilateral symmetry?
qs.s: Annelids are true coelomate, bilaterally symmetrical animals. Adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry.

qs.q:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I:
(a) 6-15 pairs of gill slits
(b) Heterocercal caudal fin
(c) Air Bladder
(d) Poison sting
Column-II:
(i) Trygon
(ii) Cyclostomes
(iii) Chondrichthyes
(iv) Osteichthyes
qs.s: Cyclostomes have 6-15 pairs of gill slits, Chondrichthyes have heterocercal tail, Osteichthyes have air bladders, and Trygon possesses a poison sting.

qs.q:
Which of the following statements are true for the phylum-Chordata ?
(a) In Urochordata notochord extends from head to tail and it is present throughout their life.
(b) In Vertebrata notochord is present during the embryonic period only.
(c) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow.
(d) Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla : Hemichordata, Tunicata and Cephalochordata.
qs.s: In Vertebrata, the notochord is present only during embryonic stages, and chordates possess a dorsal hollow CNS.

qs.q:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column-I:
(a) Gregarious, polyphagous pest
(b) Adult with radial symmetry and larva with bilateral symmetry
(c) Book lungs
(d) Bioluminescence
Column-II:
(i) Asterias
(ii) Scorpion
(iii) Ctenoplana
(iv) Locusta
qs.s: Locusta is a gregarious pest, Asterias adults are radially symmetrical with bilateral larvae, Scorpion respires via book lungs, and Ctenoplana exhibits bioluminescence.

qs.q: Bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate animals are exemplified by:
qs.s: Platyhelminthes are bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate flatworms.

qs.q: Which of the following options does correctly represent the characteristic features of phylum Annelida ?
o: Triploblastic, unsegmented body and bilaterally symmetrical.
Triploblastic, segmented body and bilaterally symmetrical.
Triploblastic, flattened body and acoelomate condition.
Diploblastic, mostly marine and radially symmetrical.
qs.s: Annelids are triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical, and possess a metamerically segmented body.

qs.q:
Match the following group of organisms with their respective distinctive characteristics and select the correct option
Organisms:
(a) Platyhelminthes
(b) Echinoderms
(c) Hemichordates
(d) Aves
Characteristics:
(i) Cylindrical body with no segmentation
(ii) Warm blooded animals with direct development
(iii) Bilateral symmetry with incomplete digestive system
(iv) Radial symmetry with Indirect development
qs.s: Platyhelminthes show incomplete digestion, adult echinoderms show radial symmetry with indirect larvae, hemichordates have unsegmented cylindrical body, and aves are warm-blooded.

qs.q: All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates, why?
o: Notochord is replaced by vertebral column in adult of some chordates.
Ventral hollow nerve cord remains throughout life in some chordates.
All chordates possess notochord throughout their life.
qs.s: In vertebrates, the embryonic notochord is replaced by a bony or cartilaginous vertebral column in adults.

qs.q:
Match the following columns and select the correct option:
Column-I:
(a) Aptenodytes
(b) Pteropus
(c) Pterophyllum
(d) Petromyzon
Column-II:
(i) Flying fox
(ii) Angel fish
(iii) Lamprey
(iv) Penguin
qs.s: Aptenodytes is penguin, Pteropus is flying fox, Pterophyllum is angel fish, and Petromyzon is lamprey.

qs.q:
Read the following statements.
(a) Metagenesis is observed in Helminths.
(b) Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate animals.
(c) Round worms have organ-system level of body organization.
(d) Comb plates present in ctenophores help in digestion.
(e) Water vascular system is characteristic of echinoderms.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
qs.s: Statements (b), (c), and (e) are correct; metagenesis occurs in cnidarians (not helminths) and comb plates function in locomotion (not digestion).

qs.q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List-I:
(a) Metamerism
(b) Canal system
(c) Comb plates
(d) Cnidoblasts
List-II:
(i) Coelenterata
(ii) Ctenophora
(iii) Annelida
(iv) Porifera
qs.s: Metamerism occurs in Annelida, canal system in Porifera, comb plates in Ctenophora, and cnidoblasts in Coelenterata.

qs.q:
Match the following:
List-I:
(a) Physalia
(b) Limulus
(c) Ancylostoma
(d) Pinctada
List-II:
(i) Pearl oyster
(ii) Portuguese Man of War
(iii) Living fossil
(iv) Hookworm
qs.s: Physalia is Portuguese Man of War, Limulus is a living fossil, Ancylostoma is hookworm, and Pinctada is pearl oyster.

qs.q: Which one of the following organisms bears hollow and pneumatic long bones?
qs.s: Neophron (vulture) is a bird possessing pneumatic hollow long bones adapted for flight.

qs.q: Nitrogenous waste is excreted in the form of pellet or paste by:
qs.s: Pavo (peacock) is a bird and excretes uricotelic waste as a dry paste or pellet.

qs.q:
Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.
Reason (R): Notochord is replaced by vertebral column in the adult vertebrates.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
qs.s: All vertebrates are chordates because they retain chordate features, but embryonic notochord gets replaced by a vertebral column in adults.

qs.q: In which of the following animals, digestive tract has additional chambers like crop and gizzard ?
qs.s: Pavo, Psittacula, and Corvus are all birds whose digestive systems include both crop and gizzard.

qs.q:
Select the incorrect statements with respect to cyclostomes:
(a) They lack scales and paired fins.
(b) They have circular mouth with jaws.
(c) They bear 6-15 pairs of gills
(d) They migrate to deep sea for spawning.
qs.s: Cyclostomes are jawless (sucking circular mouth without jaws) and migrate to fresh water for spawning, making statements (b) and (d) incorrect.

qs.q: Which of the following animals has three chambered heart?
qs.s: Chelone (turtle) is a reptile possessing a 3-chambered heart with an incompletely divided ventricle.

qs.q: Radial symmetry is NOT found in adults of phylum
qs.s: Hemichordates are bilaterally symmetrical throughout their lifecycle.

qs.q:
Select the correct statements with reference to chordates.
A. Presence of mid-dorsal, solid and double nerve cord.
B. Presence of closed circulatory system
C. Presence of paired pharyngeal gill slits
D. Presence of dorsal heart
E. Triploblastic pseudocoelomate animals
qs.s: Chordates are coelomate animals featuring a closed circulatory system and paired pharyngeal gill slits.

qs.q: The unique mammalian characteristics are:
o: pinna, monocondylic skull and mammary glands
hairs, tympanic membrane and mammary glands
qs.s: Presence of hair, external ears (pinnae), and milk-producing mammary glands are unique diagnostic features of mammals.

qs.q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Contractile vacuole
(B) Water vascular system
(C) Canal system
(D) Flame cells
List-II:
(I) Asterias
(II) Amoeba
(III) Spongilla
(IV) Taenia
qs.s: Contractile vacuole is present in Amoeba, water vascular system in Asterias, canal system in Spongilla, and flame cells in Taenia.

qs.q:
Select the correct statements:
(A) Platyhelminthes are triploblastic pseudocoelomate and bilaterally symmetrical organisms.
(B) Ctenophores reproduce only sexually and fertilization is external.
(C) In tapeworm, fertilization is internal but sexes are not separate.
(D) Ctenophores are exclusively marine, diploblastic and bioluminescent organisms.
(E) In sponges, fertilization is external and development is direct.
qs.s: Statements (B), (C), and (D) are correct; Platyhelminthes are acoelomate, and sponges show internal fertilization and indirect development.

qs.q:
Match List I with List II.
List I:
A. Pleurobrachia
B. Radula
C. Stomochord
D. Air bladder
List II:
I. Mollusca
II. Ctenophora
III. Osteichthyes
IV. Hemichordata
qs.s: Pleurobrachia is a Ctenophore, Radula is found in Mollusca, Stomochord in Hemichordata, and Air bladder in Osteichthyes.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements :-
A. Annelids are true coelomates
B. Poriferans are pseudocoelomates
C. Aschelminthes are acoelomates
D. Platyhelminthes are pseudocoelomates
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :-
qs.s: Statement A is correct because annelids are true coelomates. Poriferans are acoelomate/cellular, Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomate, and Platyhelminthes are acoelomate.

qs.q:
Match List I with List II.
List-I:
A. Pterophyllum
B. Myxine
C. Pristis
D. Exocoetus
List-II:
I. Hag fish
II. Saw fish
III. Angel fish
IV. Flying fish
qs.s: Pterophyllum is Angel fish, Myxine is Hag fish, Pristis is Saw fish, and Exocoetus is Flying fish.

qs.q:
The following are the statements about non-chordates :-
A. Pharynx is perforated by gill slits.
B. Notochord is absent.
C. Central nervous system is dorsal.
D. Heart is dorsal if present.
E. Post anal tail is absent.
qs.s: Non-chordates lack a notochord, have a ventral CNS, possess a dorsal heart when present, and lack a post-anal tail.

qs.q:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
A. Chondrichthyes
B. Cyclostomata
C. Osteichthyes
D. Amphibia
List-II:
I. Clarias
II. Carcharodon
III. Myxine
IV. Ichthyophis
qs.s: Chondrichthyes includes Carcharodon, Cyclostomata includes Myxine, Osteichthyes includes Clarias, and Amphibia includes Ichthyophis.

qs.q: Open Circulatory system is present in:
qs.s: Anopheles, Limax (mollusc), and Limulus (arthropod) possess open circulatory systems.

qs.q: Which of the following pairs is an incorrect match ?
qs.s: Platyhelminthes are triploblastic animals, not diploblastic.

qs.q:
Assertion (A): Members of subphylum vertebrate possess notochord during the embryonic period. The notochord is replaced by a cartiliaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult.
Reason (R): Thus all chordates are vertebrates but not all vertebrates are chordates.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :-
o: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
qs.s: Assertion A is true, but Reason R is false because 'all vertebrates are chordates, but not all chordates are vertebrates'.

qs.q: Which one of the following is a radially symmetrical, blind sac body plan and diploblastic animal?
qs.s: Physalia is a diploblastic coelenterate displaying radial symmetry and a blind-sac digestive plan.

qs.q: Which one is not a platyhelminthes?
qs.s: Hookworm (Ancylostoma) belongs to phylum Aschelminthes (nematodes).

qs.q:
Consider the following statements :-
(A) Protochordates are exclusively marine
(B) In cephalochordates, Notochord extends from head to tail region.
(C) In urochordates, Notochord is present only in larval tail.
(D) Cranium and vertebral column are bony in cyclostomates.
Which of the above statement is/are correct?
qs.s: Statements A, B, and C are correct. Cyclostomes lack a bony cranium and vertebral column (cartilaginous instead).

qs.q:
Consider the following characteristic of fishes:
(A) They have four pairs of gills which are covered by an operculum.
(B) They have air bladder which regulates buoyancy
(C) They are mostly viviparous and development is direct
(D) Their body is streamlined and covered with cycloid/ctenoid scales
Which of the above characteristics regarding bony fishes are correct?
qs.s: Bony fishes are mostly oviparous with indirect/direct development, making statement C incorrect.

qs.q: Which of the following animal is radially symmetrical but has a bilaterally symmetrical larva?
qs.s: Echinoderms like Asterias are radially symmetrical as adults but possess bilaterally symmetrical free-swimming larvae.

qs.q:
Identified the correct statement from the following with reference to Amphibians:
(A) They have internal fertilisation and development is direct.
(B) Amphibian skin is moist and without scales
(C) Their body is divisible into head and trunk
(D) They have three chambered heart
Select the correct answer:
qs.s: Amphibians usually undergo external fertilization and indirect development, making statement A incorrect.

qs.q:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?
(A) Poikilothemous - Birds and mammals
(B) Agnatha - Petromyzon and Myxine
(C) Tunicates - Ascidia, Salpa and Doliolum
(D) Cartilaginous fishes - Betta and Labeo
qs.s: Petromyzon and Myxine are jawless Agnatha, and Ascidia, Salpa, and Doliolum are tunicates.

qs.q: Water vascular system is found in:
qs.s: The water vascular system is a characteristic diagnostic feature of Echinodermata.

qs.q:
Match the column :-
(a) Dentalium - (iv) Tusk shell
(b) Ophiura - (i) Brittle star
(c) Antedon - (v) Sea lily
(d) Echinus - (iii) Sea Urchin
(e) Sepia - (ii) Cuttle fish
qs.s: Dentalium is tusk shell, Ophiura is brittle star, Antedon is sea lily, Echinus is sea urchin, and Sepia is cuttle fish.

qs.q: True coelom and metameric segmentation in the body is first observed in which of the following phylum?
qs.s: Metameric body segmentation combined with true coelom appeared first evolutionary in phylum Annelida.

qs.q:
Read the following statements (a to e) carefully:
(a) Triploplastic
(b) Bilateral symmetric
(c) Organ system organisation
(d) Pseudocoelomate
(e) Metameric segmentation
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct for phylum Aschelminthyes
o: a, b, c, d and e
qs.s: Aschelminthes are triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical organ-system level pseudocoelomates without metameric segmentation.

qs.q: Which of the following coelenterate exist in both forms polyp and medusa and exhibit metagenesis?
qs.s: Obelia exhibits both polypoid and medusoid generations and undergoes metagenesis.

qs.q: Mark the incorrectly matched pair
o: Petromyzon Body devoid of scales and paired fins
Scoliodon Operculum present but air bladder is absent
Exocoetus Heart two chamered with sinus venosus
Rana Cold blooded with 10 pairs of cranial nerves and mesonephric kidneys
qs.s: Scoliodon is a cartilaginous fish and lacks an operculum (gill cover).

qs.q:
Match list 'A' and List 'B' correctly and find your answer from the code given below
List-A (Animal):
(i) Physalia
(ii) Pennatula
(iii) Gorgonia
(iv) Meandrina
List-B (Common name):
(A) Brain coral
(B) Sea fan
(C) Sea pen
(D) Portuguese man of war
qs.s: Physalia is Portuguese man of war, Pennatula is sea pen, Gorgonia is sea fan, and Meandrina is brain coral.

qs.q: Which of the following is gregarious pest?
qs.s: Locusta (locust) is a destructive gregarious pest.

qs.q: Pick the odd pair out:
qs.s: Aschelminthes possess organ-system level organization, not tissue level.

qs.q: Select the group of organisms given below those have diploblastic members only:
qs.s: Aurelia, Physalia, and Meandrina are coelenterates and consist strictly of diploblastic members.

qs.q: Fresh water sponge is:
qs.s: Spongilla is a freshwater poriferan.

qs.q: The symmetry found in an animal which can be divided into indentical left and right halves in only one plane is:
qs.s: Bilateral symmetry divides an organism's body into identical left and right halves in a single median plane.

qs.q: Select the pseudocoelomates from the list of organisms given below :
qs.s: Wuchereria, Ascaris, and Ancylostoma all belong to phylum Aschelminthes and are pseudocoelomates.

qs.q: Which of the following pairs of animals comprise 'Comb jellies' ?
qs.s: Pleurobrachia and Ctenoplana belong to phylum Ctenophora, commonly known as comb jellies.

qs.q: Which one of the following pairs of animals comprise 'Cartilaginous fishes'?
qs.s: Pristis (sawfish) and Carcharodon (great white shark) are cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes).

qs.q: Which of the following fishes is also known as "Great white shark'?
qs.s: Carcharodon carcharias is commonly called the great white shark.

qs.q:
A schematic representation of a chordate's embryo is shown in the above figure. [Figure omitted]
The structures marked A, B, C and D are respectively:
o: Notochord, Nerve cord, Intestine and gill slits
Post anal part, Gill slits, Nerve cord and Notochord
Post anal part, nerve cord, Notochord and Gill
Post anal part, Notochord, Nervecord and Gill slits.
qs.s: The labeled parts of a chordate embryo correspond sequentially to post-anal tail, notochord, nerve cord, and pharyngeal gill slits.

qs.q: In which one of the following protochordates notochord present only in the tail of larva ?
qs.s: Ascidia is a urochordate where the notochord is present strictly in the larval tail.

qs.q: In which of the following group notochord present in whole life?
qs.s: In Cephalochordata (e.g., Branchiostoma), the notochord extends from head to tail and persists throughout life.

qs.q:
Match the column-I with the column-II and find out the correct answer:
Column-I:
(A) Spongocoel
(B) Dorso-ventrally flattened body
(C) Coelenteron cavity
(D) Chitinous exoskeleton
Column-II:
(i) Arthropoda
(ii) Cnidaria
(iii) Porifera
(iv) Platyhelminthes
qs.s: Spongocoel is in Porifera, dorso-ventrally flattened body in Platyhelminthes, coelenteron cavity in Cnidaria, and chitinous exoskeleton in Arthropoda.

qs.q: Which of the following is a matching pair ?
qs.s: Torpedo is correctly matched with its common name, electric ray.

qs.q: Which one is not the character of Osteichthyes?
qs.s: Placoid scales are characteristic of Chondrichthyes; Osteichthyes have cycloid or ctenoid scales.

qs.q: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
qs.s: Enterobius is pinworm; Ancylostoma is hookworm.

qs.q: The greatest evolutionary change that enabled the land vertebrates to be completely free from water, was the development of:
qs.s: Cleidoic (shelled) eggs protected developing embryos from drying out, allowing terrestrial reproduction independent of water.

qs.q: A mammal which completely lives in water is:
qs.s: Whales are aquatic mammals that reside exclusively in ocean habitats.

qs.q:
How many in the given examples of animals are Coelentrates?
Physalia, Obelia, Planaria, Pennatula, Gorgonia, Pleurobrachia, Meandrina and Nereis
qs.s: Physalia, Obelia, Pennatula, Gorgonia, and Meandrina are 5 coelenterate organisms.

qs.q: Identify the following four animals (A, B, C and D) given below. Which one of these is not correctly identified in the option given along with its correct taxonomic group and their common name ? [Figure omitted]
qs.s: Adamsia belongs to Coelenterata (Cnidaria), not Ctenophora.

qs.q:
How many organism are related with Echinodermata phylum?
Star fish, Sea-urchin, Sea-lily, Sea-mouse, Sea-hare, Sea-cucumber, Brittle star, Sea-squirt, Sea-fan, Sea-pen
qs.s: Star fish, sea-urchin, sea-lily, sea-cucumber, and brittle star make 5 echinoderms. (Key specifies 3 - option 3: 6 organisms).

qs.q: Which of the following shows the sexual dimorphism?
qs.s: Ascaris and Macaca show distinct morphologic differences between males and females (sexual dimorphism).

qs.q: Which one of the following features is common in silverfish, scorpion, dragonfly and prawn ?
o: Three pairs of legs and segmented body
Chitinous cuticle and two pairs of antennae
qs.s: All four animals are arthropods sharing jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton.

qs.q: In which animal nerve cell is present but brain is absent?
qs.s: Hydra (Cnidaria) has a non-polarized nerve net throughout its body without a central brain.

qs.q: Which one of the following is not a living fossil?
qs.s: Archaeopteryx is an extinct fossil, not a living fossil.

qs.q: Body is divisible into head and trunk in:
qs.s: Amphibians like frogs have a body divided simply into head and trunk, lacking a neck region.

qs.q: The evidence for the origin of birds from reptiles is the presence in them of:
qs.s: Presence of epidermal scales on the legs of birds provides evolutionary evidence of reptilian ancestry.

qs.q: In which one of the following groups all animals are hermaphrodite?
qs.s: Hydra, leech, and tapeworm are all monoecious (hermaphroditic) organisms.

qs.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: The most distinct feature of echinoderms is the presence of water canal system.
Statement-II: Echinodermata exhibits radial or bilateral symmetry depending on the stage.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement-I and II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
qs.s: Statement-I is incorrect because echinoderms possess a water vascular system, whereas poriferans possess a water canal system.

qs.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: In cephalochordate notochord is persistent throughout their life.
Statement-II: Branchiostoma is an example of cephalochordata
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement-I and II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
qs.s: Both statements are correct; cephalochordates feature a lifelong notochord and Branchiostoma is a key representative.

qs.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: All chordates are vertebrates but all vertebrates are not chordates.
Statement-II: Sub phylum urochordata and cephalochordate are often referred as protochordata.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement-I and II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
qs.s: Statement-I is incorrect because all vertebrates are chordates, but not all chordates are vertebrates.

qs.q:
Given below are two statements; one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Water vascular system helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food and respiration in porifera.
Reason (R): The presence of water vascular system is most unique feature of porifera.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
o: Both (A) & (R) are correct but (R) is the not correct explanation of (A).
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) & (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
qs.s: Both Assertion and Reason are false; water vascular system is characteristic of echinoderms, not porifera.

qs.q:
Match the following:
(a) Operculum - (viii) Osteichthyes
(b) Parapodia - (v) Annelida
(c) Scales - (iv) Reptilia
(d) Comb plates - (i) Ctenophora
(e) Radula - (ii) Mollusca
(f) Hairs - (vii) Mammalia
(g) Choanocytes - (iii) Porifera
(h) Gill slits - (vi) Cyclostomata and Chondrichthyes
o: a-vi, b-v, c-vii, d-i, e-ii, f-viii, g-iii, h-iv
a-viii, b-v, c-iv, d-i, e-ii, f-vii, g-iii, h-vi
a-viii, b-vii, c-vi, d-v, e-ii, f-iv, g-ii, h-i
a-i, b-vi, c-v, d-viii, e-ii, f-iii, g-iv, h-vii
qs.s: Operculum belongs to Osteichthyes, parapodia to Annelida, scales to Reptilia, comb plates to Ctenophora, radula to Mollusca, hair to Mammalia, choanocytes to Porifera, and uncovered gill slits to Cyclostomata/Chondrichthyes.

qs.q: Find incorrectly matched parasitic animal with its phylum.
qs.s: Wuchereria (filarial worm) is an Aschelminthes (nematode), not a Platyhelminthes.

qs.q: Which one of the following is a matching set of a phylum and its three examples ?
qs.s: Loligo (squid), Teredo (shipworm), and Octopus are all molluscs.

qs.q: Metameric segmentation is the characteristic of:
qs.s: Annelida and Arthropoda (along with Chordata) display metameric body segmentation.

qs.q: Two common characters found in Centipede, Cockroach and Crab are:
qs.s: As arthropods, centipedes, cockroaches, and crabs share jointed legs and a chitinous exoskeleton.

qs.q: Biradial symmetry and lack of cnidoblasts are the characteristic of:
qs.s: Ctenoplana and Beroe are ctenophores showing biradial symmetry and lacking cnidoblasts.

qs.q: In which one of the following sets of animals all the four give birth to young ones ?
qs.s: Kangaroo, Hedgehog, Dolphin, and Loris are all viviparous mammals.

qs.q: Which one of the following is a matching pair of a body feature and the animal possessing it?
o: Pharyngeal gill slits absent in embryo Chamaeleon
qs.s: Leech is an annelid possessing a ventral solid nerve cord central nervous system.

qs.q: What is true about Nereis, Scorpion, Cockroach and Silver fish ?
o: They all belong to the same phylum
They all have paired jointed appendages
qs.s: Nereis (annelid) and the arthropods all possess a dorsal heart.

qs.q: Which one of the following pairs is mismatched?
qs.s: Pearls are produced by marine pearl oysters (Pinctada), not Pila globosa.

qs.q:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched ?
Animals - Morphological features
(A) Crocodile - 4-chambered heart
(B) Sea Urchin - Parapodia
(C) Obelia - Metagenesis
(D) Lemur - Thecodont
qs.s: Crocodiles have a 4-chambered heart, Obelia exhibits metagenesis, and Lemurs have thecodont teeth.

qs.q: What is common between parrot, platypus and kangaroo ?
qs.s: Parrot (bird), platypus, and kangaroo (mammals) are all homoiothermic (warm-blooded).

qs.q: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of phylum Annelida?
qs.s: Annelids possess a true coelom (eucoelomate), not a pseudocoelom.

qs.q: Which one of the following phyla is correctly matched with its two general characteristics?
o: Arthropoda Body divided into head, thorax and abdomen and respiration by tracheae
Chordata: Notochord at some stage and separate anal and urinary openings to the outside
Echinodermata Pentamerous radial symmetry and mostly internal fertilisation
Mollusca: Normally oviparous and development through a trochophore or veliger larva
qs.s: Molluscs are typically oviparous and undergo development through trochophore or veliger larval stages.

qs.q: Ascaris is characterized by:
o: absence of true coelom but presence of metamerism
presence of neither true coelom nor metamerism
presence of true coelom but absence of metamerism
presence of true coelom and metamerism
qs.s: Ascaris (Aschelminthes) is pseudocoelomate (lacks a true coelom) and unsegmented (lacks metamerism).

qs.q:
Which one of the following groups of the three animals each is correctly matched with their one characteristic morphological feature?
Animals - Morphological feature
(1) Liver fluke, Sea anemone, Sea cucumber - Bilateral symmetry
(2) Centipede, Prawn, Sea urchin - Joined appendages
(3) Scorpion, Spider, Cockroach - Ventral solid central nervous system
(4) Cockroach, Locust, Taenia - Metameric segmentation
qs.s: Scorpion, spider, and cockroach are non-chordate arthropods possessing a ventral, solid, double nerve cord.

qs.q: Which one of the following groups of animals is bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic?
qs.s: Aschelminthes (roundworms) are triploblastic, pseudocoelomate, bilaterally symmetrical animals.

qs.q: Peripatus is a connecting link between :
qs.s: Peripatus displays characteristics of both Annelida and Arthropoda, serving as an evolutionary link between them.

qs.q: One example of animals having a single opening to the outside that serves both as mouth as well as anus is:
qs.s: Fasciola (flatworm) possesses an incomplete digestive tract with a single opening functioning as both mouth and anus.

qs.q: Which one of the following statement about all the four of Spongilla, Leech, Dolphin and Penguin is correct?
o: Penguin is homoiothermic while the remaining three are poikilothermic
Leech is a fresh water form while all others are marine
Spongilla has special collared cells called choanocytes, not found in the remaining three.
qs.s: Choanocytes (collar cells) are specialized flagellated cells present exclusively in sponges like Spongilla.

qs.q: Which one of the following animals are triploblastic?
qs.s: Flatworms (Platyhelminthes) are triploblastic, while corals and ctenophores are diploblastic and sponges lack tissue layers.

qs.q: Which one of the following statement about certain given animals is correct ?
qs.s: Roundworms (Aschelminthes) are pseudocoelomate animals.

qs.q: Crocodile and Penguin are similar to Whale and Dogfish in which one of the following features ?
o: Lay eggs and guard them till they hatch
Have gill slits at some stage
Possess a solid single stranded central nervous system
qs.s: As chordates, all four organisms develop pharyngeal gill slits at some stage of embryonic or adult life.

qs.q: Which one of the following groups of animals is correctly matched with its one characteristic feature without even a single exception ?
o: Reptilia possess 3-chambered heart with one incompletely divided ventricle
Chordata possess a mouth provided with an upper and a lower jaw
Mammalia: give birth to young ones
qs.s: All Chondrichthyes possess a cartilaginous endoskeleton without exception.

qs.q: Which one of the following animals is correctly matched with its particular named taxonomic category?
qs.s: Panthera tigris: tigris represents the specific epithet/species name.

qs.q:
In which one of the following the genus name, its two character and its class/phylum are correctly matched?
Genus name - Two characters - Class/Phylum
(1) Ascaris - Body segmented, Males and females distinct - Annelida
(2) Salamandra - A tympanum represents ear, Fertilization is external - Amphibia
(3) Pteropus - Skin possesses hair, Oviparous - Mammalia
(4) Aurelia - Cnidoblasts, Organ level of organization - Coelenterata
qs.s: Salamandra is an amphibian possessing a tympanum for hearing and undergoing external fertilization.

qs.q: The figure shows four animals (a), (b), (c) and (d). Select the correct answer with respect to a common characteristics of two of these animals. [Figure omitted]
o: (a) and (d) respire mainly through body wall
qs.s: Animals (c) (Pheretima) and (d) (Pila) both possess a true coelom.

qs.q:
In which one of the following, the genus name, its two characters and its phylum are not correctly matched, whereas the remaining three are correct?
Genus name - Two characters - Phylum
(1) Sycon - Pore bearing, Canal system - Porifera
(2) Periplaneta - Jointed appendages, Chitinuous exoskeleton - Arthropoda
(3) Pila - Body segmented, Mouth with Radula - Mollusca
(4) Asterias - Spiny skinned, Water vascular system - Echinodermata
qs.s: Pila (mollusc) has an unsegmented body, making option 3 incorrect.

qs.q: Which one of the following categories of animals, is correctly described with no single exception in it?
o: All sponges are marine and have collared cells
All mammals are viviparous and possess diaphragm for breathing
All reptiles possess scales, have a three chambered heart and are cold blooded (poikilothermal)
All bony fishes have four pairs of gills and an operculum on each side
qs.s: All bony fishes (Osteichthyes) feature four pairs of gills covered by an operculum on each side.

qs.q: Which one of the following pairs of animals are similar to each other pertaining to the feature stated against them?
o: Sea horse and Flying fish - Cold blooded (poikilothermal)
Garden lizard and Crocodile - Three chambered heart
qs.s: Sea horse (Hippocampus) and flying fish (Exocoetus) are both fishes and poikilothermic.

qs.q: One of the representatives of Phylum Arthropoda is:
qs.s: Silver fish (Lepisma) is an insect belonging to phylum Arthropoda.

qs.q: Which group of animals belong to the same phylum?
qs.s: Prawn, scorpion, and locusta all belong to phylum Arthropoda.

qs.q: Infection of Ascaris usually occurs by:
o: drinking water containing eggs of Ascaris
qs.s: Infection with Ascaris lumbricoides occurs through ingesting food or water contaminated with embryonated eggs.

qs.q: Which of the following are correctly matched with respect to their taxonomic classification?
o: Spiny anteater, sea urchin, sea cucumber-Echinodermata
House fly, butterfly, tsetsefly, silverfish Insecta
qs.s: House fly, butterfly, tsetsefly, and silverfish are all insects belonging to class Insecta.

qs.q:
Match the name of the animal (column-I), with one characteristics (column-II), and the phylum/ class (column-III) to which it belongs :
Column I - Column II - Column III
(1) Adamsia - radially symmetrical - Porifera
